issue_context.title: Add zeroconf discovery to Daikin
issue_context.body:
Home Assistant supports proposing a config flow to users based on zeroconf discovery. This is done based by specifying [zeroconf in your manifest](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/creating_integration_manifest#zeroconf) and adding a config flow step `async_step_zeroconf`.

Once discovered, we can ask the user to confirm if they want to set it up

Daikin was just reported in our [gathered Zeroconf services](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/27371#issuecomment-617938517) and should be made discoverable.

review_comments:
It looks like you are using the `mac` for the unique id above 👍  `await self.async_set_unique_id(mac)`

Is the mac address in the `discovery_info` ?

> Is the mac address in the discovery_info ?

No it is not, that is why we are using `CONF_HOST`..
If the host is an ip address it may change. We don't want to use ip addresses for unique id.

> If the host is an ip address it may change. We don't want to use ip addresses for unique id.

So how should I approach it?
Use something that is stable and unique to identify the device from the discovery info.

This is the only thing available: 
```
{'host': '10.0.0.6', 'port': 80, 'hostname': 'DaikinAP34738.local.', 'type': '_dkapi._tcp.local.', 'name': 'DkApi._dkapi._tcp.local.', 'properties': {'_raw': {'reg': b'eu', 'type': b'aircon', 'ver': b'1_2_51', 'adp_kind': b'3'}, 'reg': 'eu', 'type': 'aircon', 'ver': '1_2_51', 'adp_kind': '3'}}
```

I think `DaikinAP34738.local` is unique enugh.
You know the integration and device best.
Does `DaikinAP34738` remain the same when the ip changes?
I don't know, my Daikin unit doesn't support zeroconf.
@TopdRob what is your take on this?
Yes it stays unique. It's the SSID of the access point mode.
Since the user can't change this, seems stable enough to me.
We didn't change to `"hostname"` key before merge.
